items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: we also did The Milton Berle Show

ctx.x: which we toured quite extensively. And I stayed with Louis' band right up until December... Well, actually, in the latter part of December, Louis Jordan decided to disband the band, to break the band up. From what I understood, I was told at that particular time that he had made so much money til he was actually only getting about 5 cents out of every dollar he made! So he decided to break the band up.

But before that, we did a thing of recording for... I don't remember the record company we did it for. I think it was Decca. But we recorded for about a week, which included about, I guess, at least 18 or 20 sides, if I can remember, of just about everything that he'd ever done. He re-recorded a lot of the things. And while we were in New York, I think, we also did The Milton Berle Show, which was a very big show on television. So it wound up being a very successful thing.

During that period, I had the pleasure of working with some musicians that I made friends with for life. One of them was a fellow everybody calls Christopher Columbus -- Chris Columbo. He is a drummer, and I guess Chris should be in his middle seventies or close to eighty years old -- I understand he's still playing in Atlantic City. He had a very unique way of playing. The seat that he used when he played drums was a motorcycle seat, and he jumped up and down, which was a very attractive thing to people when…
